Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map
Project Summary: Mars missions face extreme temperatures, dust storms, rugged terrain, and communication delays. Astronauts need reliable data to navigate safely, avoid hazards, and locate research sites.
Our Solution: An interactive 3D mapping platform integrating NASA geological and topographical data into a unified Martian globe for terrain inspection and independent layer toggling.
NASA Data Integration: Standardizes NASA datasets across formats:
- HiRISE: High-resolution surface/obstacle imagery.
- CTX: Regional navigational context imagery.
- MOLA: Elevation data for terrain analysis.
- THEMIS: Thermal/infrared surface observations.
- SHARAD: Subsurface radar for buried structures/ice.
Technical Implementation: Modular architecture using React and TypeScript for the 3D globe frontend, with Python and FastAPI powering backend APIs and geospatial processing.
Navigation & Terrain Analysis: Uses elevation data and A* pathfinding to evaluate slopes, craters, and rocks, assigning traversal costs for safe routing.
Innovation & Impact: Unifies fragmented planetary datasets into one human-centric interface for route planning, hazard detection, and site selection.
Future Scope: AI terrain classification, obstacle detection, dust-storm tracking, rover telemetry, and offline map access.
Conclusion: Combines NASA data, 3D visualization, and hazard-aware routing into a vital digital companion for Mars exploration.

Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

1. Project Overview

Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is an interactive 3D Mars exploration platform designed to help future astronauts understand the Martian surface, identify potential hazards, and plan safer exploration routes. The project brings together geographical, topographical, geological, and scientific information from NASA missions into a unified mapping environment. Instead of exploring different datasets separately, users can visualize and compare available information through a single interactive interface.

2. Problem Statement

Human exploration of Mars will involve several challenges, including extreme temperatures, rocky terrain, steep slopes, craters, dust storms, and limited communication with Earth. Astronauts will need accurate information about their surroundings before travelling to unfamiliar locations. However, planetary data is collected by different missions and instruments, often in different formats and resolutions. Accessing and understanding this information together can be difficult. Our project aims to simplify this process by providing an integrated Martian map that makes scientific and geographical data easier to explore and interpret.

3. Proposed Solution

We are developing a web-based 3D Mars globe that allows users to explore the planet, zoom into specific regions, inspect surface features, and switch between different geographical and scientific layers. The platform is designed to combine multiple NASA datasets into one environment, helping users understand terrain conditions and geographical characteristics. Its primary focus is to support astronaut navigation, scientific exploration, and mission planning.

4. NASA Data Sources

The platform is designed to integrate data from several NASA missions and instruments:

  • HiRISE: Provides high-resolution images for examining detailed surface features, rocks, and geological formations.
  • CTX: Provides wider regional imagery to understand the surrounding landscape.
  • MOLA: Supplies elevation measurements for topographical visualization and terrain analysis.
  • THEMIS: Provides thermal and infrared observations to study surface properties and temperature variations.
  • SHARAD: Uses subsurface radar observations to investigate buried geological structures and possible underground ice.
    Combining these datasets provides a more comprehensive understanding of the Martian environment.

5. Key Features

  • Interactive 3D Mars Globe: Explore Mars through a three-dimensional interface with zooming, navigation, and geographical inspection.
  • Layer-Based Visualization: Switch between available satellite imagery and scientific datasets to examine different aspects of the Martian surface.
  • Terrain Understanding: Use elevation and topographical information to understand surface variations and identify potentially challenging regions.
  • Scientific Exploration: Examine craters, geological formations, and other locations that may be valuable for scientific investigation.
  • Mission Planning Support: Provide geographical context that can help astronauts evaluate destinations and plan exploration activities.
  • Expandable Architecture: Allow additional NASA datasets and scientific layers to be integrated as the platform develops.

6. Technical Architecture

The application uses a modular web architecture:

  • Frontend: React and TypeScript for the interactive user interface and application components.
  • 3D Visualization: A globe-based rendering system for displaying the Martian surface and geographical layers.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI for API communication, backend services, and data processing.
  • Geospatial Processing: Organizing geographical and scientific datasets for consistent visualization and spatial analysis.
  • Layer Management: Managing individual map layers independently so that datasets can be loaded and displayed as required.

7. Navigation and Safety

A major objective is to make future Martian exploration safer. Elevation and terrain information can help identify steep slopes, crater boundaries, and potentially difficult regions. The system can incorporate pathfinding algorithms such as A* to calculate routes between selected locations. By considering distance and terrain-related traversal costs, route planning can move beyond simply finding the shortest path and instead consider safety and mission requirements.

8. Innovation and Impact

The main innovation is bringing multiple types of Martian scientific information into one interactive environment designed around human exploration. Rather than presenting isolated satellite images, the platform aims to make different datasets accessible through a unified layered map. It can support future astronaut navigation, terrain assessment, geological investigation, scientific site selection, and mission preparation.

9. Future Scope

Future improvements may include AI-powered terrain classification, automatic crater and obstacle detection, advanced slope analysis, hazard-aware route optimization, dust-storm and environmental monitoring, rover telemetry integration, and offline map access. These capabilities could make the platform more useful for astronauts operating in remote areas with limited communication.

10. Conclusion

Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map aims to turn complex and distributed Martian scientific data into a practical exploration tool. By combining NASA mission datasets, interactive 3D visualization, geospatial information, and navigation-oriented capabilities, the project seeks to help future explorers better understand the Martian landscape, identify potential hazards, plan efficient journeys, and discover scientifically valuable locations.
